Ravi P: Quick RFC follow-up: do we treat app-submitted rollouts as authoritative or as "intent" that platform reconciles?

Lina K: Strong +1 for intent. Platform should enforce global safety (capacity, SLAs), apps declare intent only (pct, gates, fallbacks).

Omar G: Intent model avoids tenant-by-tenant divergence. Proposed flow: app POSTs intent -> planner produces plan with actual cohort assignment -> planner publishes seq-numbered decision that hosts consume.

Sania R: Hosts need a local escape hatch. Example: if p95 balloons or GPU memory spikes, host flips to fallback immediately. But we must bound that local flip so it doesn't conflict with planner. TTL + backoff seems right.

Ravi P: Agreed. How about these primitives?
- intent fields: {pct:int, primary:string, fallbacks:[string], gates:[{metric,op,value}] }
- plan record: {assignments, seq, effective_until}

Lina K: Keep JSON examples light in Slack, but good. For safety, planner should mark assignment leases (effective_until). Hosts must only honor decisions with seq > last_seen and within effective window.

Omar G: Local fallback contract idea: when host triggers, it emits a short-lived token to central telemetry: {host, reason_code, seq_when_triggered, ttl=30s}. Planner aggregates these and can either 1) ignore transients or 2) accelerate plan if many hosts report same reason.

Sania R: Reason codes please: CPU_STALL, OOM, NET_ERR, KV_MISS, SLOW_MODEL. That will help postmortems. Also include optional "stack" field for debug (but not required in telemetry).

Ravi P: Hysteresis: local fallback should use exponential backoff on re-enable attempts (e.g., start 5s, double up to 2m). Planner-level rollbacks use consecutive-window thresholds (default 3 windows).

Lina K: Metrics window defaults? Planner opts for 60s windows, EWMA smoothing alpha=0.2 by default. Make tunable in intent but require approval for <30s.

Omar G: API surfaces to define:
- POST /intents -> returns intent_id
- GET /plans/{intent_id} -> current plan + seq
- GET /assignments?host={id} -> host's current assignment + seq
- POST /plans/{id}/override -> ops-only with RBAC token
- ws /events/planner-stream -> read-only stream for SRE

Sania R: Add audit rules: every intent change stores user, diff, client_request_id. Overrides must be logged with who/why. Also require two-person approve for intents >20% by default.

Ravi P: Edge cases: what if planner unavailable? Hosts should continue honoring last good plan and continue local fallback rules. Sequence numbers prevent replays when planner recovers.

Lina K: One more: plan garbage-collection. Plans should include effective_until and we GC after TTL + grace window (default 5m) to avoid stale plans lingering.

ops-bot: Planner applied plan 1854321000 at 2026-03-23T16:02Z (seq=42) :white_check_mark:

Omar G: I'll prototype the seq-check + TTL logic in the host-side shim (small lib used by agent).

Sania R: I'll author the reason_code enum and backoff guidance in the runbook.

Lina K: I'll draft the intent -> plan reconciliation doc and the minimal API schema. Draft by Fri.

Ravi P: Perfect. We'll consolidate into RFC follow-up and add RBAC/audit tickets. Thanks.
